sections.html:
Wheat Ridge is a small home rule city in Jefferson County, directly west of Denver. Its municipal center is about 8.5 miles west-northwest of the state capitol, where Interstate 70 meets State Highway 391. The city covers roughly 9.6 square miles at 5,348 feet and is hemmed in by Arvada, Lakewood, Edgewater, Denver, Golden and other neighbors, so a Wheat Ridge house tends to be compared with homes in the surrounding suburbs as well as with others in town.

The 2020 census counted 32,398 residents and 15,471 housing units, of which 5.2 percent were vacant. Median age was 41.1, and 20.6 percent of residents were 65 or older. Heirs and downsizing owners are therefore common sellers, and many want the house sold without prep work.

sections.h2: The Carnation City and its older houses
sections.html:
Wheat Ridge began as a rest stop during the Gold Rush of the late 1850s and was farming country, known as the Carnation City, by the mid 1900s. Orchards and crop fields dominated until the 1960s. During the 1950s, housing for the Denver workforce filled the unincorporated parts of Jefferson County, and pressure from neighboring cities to annex that land pushed residents to incorporate in 1969.

The city is mostly built out today, with houses from the postwar decades on lots that were once farm fields. The James H. Baugh House, an 1860 log cabin, is on the National Register of Historic Places and stands in Wheat Ridge Historic Park.

sections.h2: Do creeks and gulches affect a Wheat Ridge sale?
sections.html:
Clear Creek runs east and then northeast through the city. Lena Gulch, a tributary, crosses the southwest part, and small lakes and reservoirs sit along both waterways: Crown Hill Lake, Kestrel Pond and North Henry Lee Reservoir in the south-central area, and West Lake, Tabor Lake and Prospect Lake in the west-central area.

Water views help a listing, but buyers will ask about drainage and flood zones. If your lot is near Clear Creek or Lena Gulch, gather any flood or drainage paperwork before you list.

A license is required for short-term rentals in Wheat Ridge, and whole-home licenses are capped in each of the four council districts. The ordinance took effect May 1, 2021. The city also collects a 10 percent lodgers' tax on completed reservations, due on the 20th of each month. The cap equals 2 percent of single-family and two-unit dwellings in a district.

  • Whole-home maximums are 49 in District I, 52 in District II, 54 in District III and 37 in District IV.
  • As of the city's February 2026 count, only District III had openings, with 9 left. Other districts had waitlists, led by 35 names in District I.
  • Only the legal owner can apply, and a new purchase requires a copy of the deed.
  • Licenses cannot be transferred, so a buyer cannot take over yours.
  • Owner-occupied partial-home rentals fall outside the cap.

This matters most when your buyer plans a whole-home rental in a district with no licenses left, since that buyer joins a waitlist. The rules are on the City of Wheat Ridge Short Term Rentals page, and questions go to license@wheatridge.gov. If you have been renting the house short term, tell the buyer plainly that your license does not pass with the property, and keep any lodgers' tax filings current until the closing date.

sections.h2: Can I keep gardens, bees and chickens on a residential lot?
sections.html:
City Council passed Ordinance 1491 in May 2011 to support urban agriculture. Owners may grow and sell produce and keep animals such as bees and chickens, within city rules. Urban gardens, community gardens included, are allowed in every zone district. Farmers' markets are allowed everywhere except residential areas where the main use is a single or two-family home, and they need a business license. Produce stands need one too, and on residential property they must follow the home occupation rules.

Got a garden bed, a coop or a hive? Tell the buyer what is on the lot and how you have handled the city's requirements.

sections.h2: When Jefferson County property taxes are due
sections.html:
Payment optionDue date
First installmentFebruary 28, or the next business day if the county is closed
Full paymentApril 30
Second installmentJune 15

One notice arrives by the end of January, with coupons for each due date. Taxes are collected in arrears, so each bill covers the previous year. Delinquent notices go out in July, so a tax bill that is behind should be taken to a title company well before then. Unpaid real property taxes are advertised in a local newspaper for three consecutive weeks starting in early October, and the annual online tax lien sale happens in November.

The Treasurer's office is at 100 Jefferson County Parkway in Golden, open Monday to Thursday from 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. and closed Fridays. The phone number is 303-271-8330, and the schedule is on the Jefferson County Treasurer's Important Dates page.

sections.h2: What a cash sale looks like for a Wheat Ridge homeowner
sections.html:
With no mortgage involved, a cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and approval. You review an offer, say yes or no, and pick a closing date with the title company.

  • The house sells as is, with no repair list.
  • You set a closing date that suits your move.
  • If the house is a rental, sort out the lease and any rental license questions beforehand.
  • The title company records the deed with Jefferson County.

Some owners are glad to avoid showings and open houses, and a cash sale has neither.

The order of events is short. We make a written offer after learning about the house. When you accept, the title company checks ownership and any lender payoff, and then you sign at closing. Unpaid taxes, if there are any, come out of the proceeds, so a past-due bill does not stop the sale.

sections.h2: Preparing a Wheat Ridge house for a quick sale
sections.html:
You do not need to renovate, but a few hours of organizing help. Pull together your latest tax notice, the mortgage servicer's number and any lease. If your lot has a garden structure, coop or hive, jot down what is there. If the property is near Clear Creek or Lena Gulch, add the drainage papers.

Heirs often ask what to do with belongings. A cash buyer purchasing as is does not need the house emptied or cleaned first, though you should remove anything of sentimental or financial value before closing. Ask the title company who is authorized to sign when an estate is involved, and ask early so the date does not slip.

faqs.q: How many people live in Wheat Ridge, Colorado?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 32,398 residents. The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 32,081.

faqs.q: When are Jefferson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due the last day of February, moving to the next business day when the office is closed. Full payment is due April 30 and the second half June 15. The county sends one notice in January.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in Wheat Ridge?
faqs.a: Only with a license. Whole-home licenses are capped by council district, and as of February 2026 only District III had any left. Licenses are non-transferable, and only the legal owner can apply.

faqs.q: Does Wheat Ridge allow backyard chickens and bees?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's urban agriculture ordinance, adopted in 2011, lets homeowners keep animals such as bees and chickens within city rules. Check the current rules before you list or buy.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Wheat Ridge house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as is, so you do not need to fix the roof, kitchen or flooring first.
